The god of Abraham The fear god of Isaac, & the Strength of Israil. Even the god, & father, of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. Hose:11:3 Taught me, whilst I was yet young, he taught me to goe, leading me by the arms in footsteps as yt I knew not,( yet knew I not that he lead me),But after when more of Age he taught me Step by Step, how I Should walke, In a Child like obedience to his ☞divine Atributes with large leadings in his mercyfull nature - love; and gave me large Experience, of his Mercyfull. love, & to greatly to accquiesce. In all his wise dispensations, teaching me, that his wisdom, knew wt was best, & his Fatherly love was so great, as all should work togeth.Rom:8:28:
☞ for good, to them asyt love him & are Called, or purposed there unto; And altho his teachings, I for many yeares Concealed it, & so Intended; yet since Collecting, what use it might be for my Self & others, I was much Pressed upon in Spirit, to write it downe,(& since by some others) for the bett. Reception, of what furthder manifestation, ye Lord now in these later dayes has declared to me (yet not for my Self only, but for others also, therefore not willing to hide it in a Napkin, well knowing that ye Same Spirit as lead me, is but one spirit & will teach all yt doe but Adhere thereunto, for god, is the same as he was yesterday, today, & so for Ever, who at Heb:1:1:Sundry times, & in divers manners, Spake unto ye Fathers ye Prophets, hath now in these last times spake to us by his sonne whome he hath made heire of all things, putting althings under him, spoiling all Principalities &
This page is blank.
Heb:2 8& powers. for, in that he put all in Subjection under him, he left ☞nothing yt is not put under him, but now we see not yet all things put under himbut we see Jesus, Crowned, with glory & honour yt at the name of Jesus, the Saviour, yt Saveth his people Phil:2 10-11 from their sins, every knee; all homage glory & honour & Obedience, of things in heaven & things in yt Earth & thingsunder ye Earth, %to whom be glory & honour %and every tongue shuld confesse that Jesus is Lord to ye glory of god the fatherdominion & praise now, henceforth, &Eternally:(& as I have said)I was Taught when I was young; ye boughs when young & tender, will yeild Easily, So it is with ye tender Soule befor it growes old in Sin, & surely as the first fruits & firstling of the flock god Required should be offerred & sacrificed to him, so is the First of our age & as it is the most acExceptable to god, so it is most easie to man, haveing not Such loads of guilt. If the Accuser About ye tenth year of my ageshould Attempt, to Awaken: it is I say much easyer, yet not all easy.

[four dots in diamond] it was not any perticuler sin: But as all sin: yet remembered none. but a strang frame to have killed my self.For about ye tenth yeare of my age, I found somthing to Awaken a sense of ye Naturof Sin,[four dots in diamond] evento dispaire of mercy which alas or at least to Question whetherI Could Expect mercy,(which alas noe, not man in the gall, but it is himself, in man, his breath ☜ Gen: 2 vr:7☞of Liveing soule, as he Comes to bring up, throughew, & from ye fall) but soone was stayed with davids praising god, in 30 Psalm:1:2:3.(I will Extoll ye O Lord)In heareing A Sermon onf it, so yt my Sorrow Echoed Joy; yn in another Sermon I Learnt watchfulness at all times,(least Satan Should get Advantage over me) 2: Corin: cap: 2: vps: 11Even to watch ye use of things, lawfull, or any appearance of Evil; all wch I still Acknowledg, First from god, Secondarily much was sucked in from, pious parents, & Religious Education, wth which by Precepts and Examples, I have accustomed my Self to pray: (& About ye 15th yeare of my ye 15 yeare of my ageage, for my Incouragement thereunto: I atained by Prayer, a promise to ☜Answer yt prayer: Declairing to me how, & by what Efects, I should know ☞yt, that prayer Should be Answered, which was fulfilled at its Apointed ☞Season; & haveing had such Experience, how god hath heard & in heareing answered; it did for the future Incouraged me, in all ye Pressurs of my soule to power qout my Request unto him, who has Required it, yt we should Call ☜upon him, in the day of trouble, & hath also Promised he will deliver, & wee must then gloryfy him, & wee doe best gloryfy him in Beleiveing unto ☞Obedience. And About the 18th yeare of my age Seeing the Strict Practice 18 yeareof some, it much Awakened in me a Serious Search, how it was with my Soule, & to what end I was borne, & to wot End I ought to live, & finding Little to Accuse my Self of sins of comission, I inquired into sins of ☞Omission, & in Scripture Record, I found that Danieldavidniel Prayed three times A day Danill: 6: vr: 10:13& david said Seaven times A day I praise three (which Certaine number mayThessalo Chap 5 16:17:18Signified many times, in ye Thessalonians.: it is said Rejoyce in ye lord Always pray wthout ceasing but Psallms: 119 164: vr.I thought it only Referred to set times, which accordingly (with all privasie), Yet dou I thi as David prayed seven set times a day for so he sems to menshantion Eving & morning I prevent ye night waches: ps: 119: 14 at mignigt will I arise & praise ye 119:26. I prevent ye dawning of ye morning. psa: 119: 147:&c.I begun, but my mouth was Stopped, like one Struk dumb, wch ☞Caused great consternachan, & terror, Saying within my Self, have I so many Sins, & Can I beg pardon for none, & so many graces doe I stand in neede of & is there not any one grace I Can ask for; yet still did I remaine as one Stupified & dumb, but filled with an awakened horror & greif, even to High despare, which soone was stilled, with an Inward Reflection, I ☞was nothing & Could doe nothing, not think in my heart to god, without divine Asistance, &, his Asistance makes our AcExceptance.

Severall disturbing objections, but still I was Answered to study duty, rather ☞then Reward, teaching me that tho: I Could not Read his secret will whether he would save me, yet I Could Read his Revealed will wch was that I should serve him; & so in his Strength I Resolved to throw my self on him, in the simple, sincere, Childlike obedience, & I If I perished it should be in so doing, which Reminded me of the 2 Kings Chap:7: v: 4:men that went into the Camp of the AssSyrians; If they set there at the gate they see nothing but death, Attend them: & If the Assyrians saved them alive they should live, & If they killed them they Could but dye. this then was my Cause, & these words waeres my Instructer & good was that god; like an Anchor of hope, to help & draw this to him.

☞I Continued, praying hearing and Reading, but often was the Returne of Sorrows, least I should labour in vaine, & little was applyed byto me, from A Sermon or Reading but Repoofe,(thrugh the Awakned Scence of Sin) as If he spake it to none but me, putting far off all Comfort.

And in some fen-months I was seized by sickness, & something dangerous, as for my owne parte, (Being before A stranger to to sickness) I did not Question but I should dye, which Caused me to mourne & weep to them wth me telling them, I had noe Asurance of a Better life, & now I feared I was to dye, for I had lived 18 1/2 yearsLong time in sin. (Being About Eighteen years & a half ould) yn Some of them said to me that I had been well Educated & in all sobriety brought up, not knowing nor so much as heard of the vanities that most then walked in; I Answered it is trueew I have been well Instructed & did Practice, what I was Capable of; when I was A Child I did loved to pray with my Sister, and to heare her pray & I did like to Read good bookes & ye Bible, as for other bookes I thought it not worth my Time &paines. & I said further I knew not any one sin yt I Lived in ☜& this was some stay, but it soone went off, & I said all this is nothing, I did but like a Child, little understanding what I did but o my sins are very many.

A few dayes after this: all my sins were laid before me,yet noe won perticuler sin remembered that all the sins of my whole life was like one act of sin, & that hell was the Receve me, & the hottest place I said, I had deserved, & I see like hell opened to me: A great, black darck pitt, & I at the brinck Ready to goe in, & I ☞ackknowledged to the lord, that he was very Just If he did Cast me in & also that he was very mercyfull in keeping me out so long, In the Land of the liveing, I Concluded and said that now hell was my portion, & god was to be praised for his long forbearance to the ☞Children of men, for he had been a Just god If he had Cast me into hell as soone as I was borne, for I had been Conceived in Sin & be Brought forth in iniquity: And as the lord taught me he was just & mercyfull, so he made me, to Consider his power \\ Horabellwhether he was not able to save me out of this\\ pit, tho I had deserved it, I did veryly beleive god was able to save me, tho. I was at the very Brinck of hell, Just agoeing in, but whether [angled ladder] it wasgod was willing to save me, this I feared, & thus Continued, A day or two; then It[angled ladder]wasthe lord Answered me that If he was not as willing aswell as able none would have been saved, for it iwas only by
By free grace that we are Saved, & how dost thou know but god will save thee,(I said who(?) me? yes thee, I said I have nothing that is good in me, a poore sinfull Creature, what is there in me, yt god should pardon me, then I was Answerd it is true nothing is in thee, but the lord spake with power, I will ☜have mercy, because I will have mercy, & because mercy pleaseth me, & I have pardoned they sins freely, & will Remember them nomore, most gladly did I Receive this word: it put more joy& gladness in my heart, then they when there Corne & oyle & wine Increaseth, & as before I sawee like hell open for me, ☞so now I see the heavens open, & an angell in the heavens Ready to Receive me, I had some Questioning of this, how I Could Expect such Mercy as this, being not worthy, I was answered if god stayed to shew mercy till we were worthy to Resceive, we should never have Mercy. Some Objections to the like purpose, but all were Answered, & so ☜Answered, as never to Question his love, nor the tempter Could never set footing to disturb my peace, & Comfort never since, but once I said wn sin wrestled within methe woman, as Esau & Jacob I tooke up Rebekah's speech. If it be so why am I thus, If the lord hath pardoned [sideways ladder] to mack me s speake: unadvisedly tho: not sinfulyme, & graciously Exaccepted me why, then, doth sin still strive to over-☜-come me,[sideways ladder] then I have looked back or calling to mind how god Came in by A mighty hand & strong arme, & Pulled me out of the Clawes of Sathan & Brought me from the gates of hell,(the way to heaven is by the gates of hell. Andthen considering, how the lord spake peace & scilenced all my doubteings % & such lick these reme[m]bar maid, my sperit say: it is so, tho I am thus: & how he freely Exaccepted, & as the Raptures as I then had,% & how willing yea even long to be with Xt which was best of all, to see that Xt which I had now but a taste of, to see him face to face: but had some desire after this to live to Gloryfy god that I might shew forth his praise yt had done so much for me, but the lord told me he was all glorious in him self, & needed not any Creature to set forth his glory, then I thought what was I, god had many in the world that he Could make use of to set forth his glory to declare it to the world though I might be called out of it, & I I said ye Lord hath Carried me one from Heb: 13:18 39:Psal:7:42 Psa:2:-strength to strength &a as he hath begun a good worke, & hath gone one so hee & will prosperPerfect it to ye Day of Redemshan he is the same, yesterday, today, & the same forever.

And now lord what wiat I for my Expectations is from thee, my soule Longeth for thee, for the liveing god when shall I come & appeare before god, O the wicked mens dread, thay Call for the mountains to fall one them, & the hills to Cover them, but o the sight of god is the heaven of heavens, those that waite & Expect such things as these what manner of men & women ought we to be In all godlyness & honnesty; how Exact In our words, lay a watch on our lips put A Bridle to our tongue y wee sin not with our mouth, how should wee as Christ, goe About doeing good, when god hath Converted strengthean ouer Bretheren we should Communicate of our Experience to others, we should not want grace by this, but wee should Increase our graces, noe Company but leaves loath some; some savor of good there , strive to season it, O ye sins of omission ☞how hard it is not to be guilty of Omitting Duties, as is Required of Every man, In there severall stations And Conditions, besides the duties we Omit between god & ye soule wh[e]n as it is our duty, nay it is our Privaledge & happyness, as god will heare & ExAccept o[ur] prayers that he should let us
us Converse with him And meditate one him, that he will permit us to fetch A turne in heaven, and thatevery day that we may be in heaven by meditation as it were before our time, that we may receive the first fruits of our spirituall Caanan, in this life:Psal. that in keeping gods Commandements there is great Reward, even ☞in this life, as well as Eternal Happyness, & Injoyment of god for ever, after this life, (nay the Comfort a Child of god Injoyes in this life, in god; will make Amends for any Afflictions he undergoeth for god, but that he will give them Eternall mercies, forver where there shall be no End, but they shall praise god to the longest line of Eternity:
O the height of this mercy O the length, O the breadth & depth of Xt love, who is able to Comprehend it, to know the love of Christ, as passeth Knowledge.

Thus for ten yeares or more, I was lead as in a Land of love being much accompanied with Joy & peace, & often in meditations: as I was Carried forth, to various subjects, somtimes of the love of god, sometimes of the vanitie of the Creature, othertimes meditated of the unsutableness of all things of this world, so Could no wayes be satisfieding to A heavenly desireing soule, & sometimes & the most usual meditations & Admirashaneing, was of the love mercy & pitty of god to fallen man, so that I was, as one yt Could see nothing but love, & in all Could desire nothing but to be swallowed up in him & to be taken to him, which earnest desire was hard to be subdued; to be Contented to wait my Appointed time till my Change Come. ☞Many great & Eminent answers of Prayer) scarce anything as ever Asked in prayer; but was Answered he never gave me A desire to ask but hee alwayes had a hand to give, & answered what he would doe☞ & I did often know when I should not ask by being straitned and Could not; so that by freedome to prayer, or a Restraint not to pray, I knew his will: & all tho. I found it my dutie to ask yet offered up my desire alwayes to his will, not daring to have any will, tho Indeed my Request was all for spiritualls, whether it was for my self or others as for the things of the world, I willingly did not take thought for ye things of the morrow; of this, much might be written, but I foreare. &as I said) About the end of ten or Eleaven yeares, some difficulties I was to pass therrongh, I still beareing up, but after In some time the sorrow prevailed, & I(not haveing skill to stand fast in the Christian Armour) was as one taken out of a land of peace: I felt it at the same houre th:3:1667:4even to A minute, how I was taken out of the peace & Rest and ☞Em[m]ediately put into A wilderness, to be tempted where I was to fight my way through, & with the three great Enimies of man, viz the world the flesh & the dievel, & as soone as by faith & prayer one seemed to be weakned, A second did arise up, so that I had noe & as soone as that temptation seemed to be overcome, A third did arise up, so that I had noe time to goe off my watch and Even fainted threwough long waiting, & Wthen I did think, & sometimes hope they were dead, then an unexpected one would Awaken so that at length,(by Experience), when I found A Sweet Calme,☜ I knew it was a Cordial before some storm of trialls In the wilderness
Where, the world the flesh & the divel maintained a Continual war ☞yet did I never Question my former Comforts, neither was I at all without great teaching, & Joy in god: in vissions of the night when Asleep & some few in the day, which alwayes taught & declared what I was to pass through.

And thus was I Carried on about ten yeares more, & neer the end of the ☞yeares I felt some great thing was to be knowne & Injoyed, but I knew not what, & I had a hungringe desire to know further of god, & how I might understand aright, how to worship him, as hee Required, And that I might Rightly, apprehend ye Intercession of Christ for us ☞& how, he was our Advocate with the father & how, I should direct prayher to god, therrow Christ, which I searched out in the scriptures but Could not understand, it, as I did beleive, it might be knowne but was Extream, Scencsible of my owne Ignorance, how little I knew of god, & how Ignorant of my self, even as one knowing nothing.☜ And as I had neere ten yeares desired a Redeption to my former state, tho: I was much stayed & Comforted; but I found there was greater Interuption in my thoughts then I had, had formerly, & I did greatly press for the dayes of old, saying O that it were as in the dayes of old when the Candle of the lord did shine Round About me when I set under his shadow, with great delight; O when will thou Restore unto me the Joyes & stillness of thy love;

After this for my support, in June the 23th 1678AB A Yeare of Jubele was Proclaimed & Proviphesied to me by an angel, or speiritIn Dream or vision, & after Affirmed by another angel in such a like Dreame, which was s they had said &, at the time performed to me, which was at the End of six months, Being Decem5b:23:1678 But About A month or three weekes before; I was Brought to that, as to ☞be fully Contented to take up my Cross dayly if it was his will, being satisfied to wait ye good Pleasure of god, not desireing, deliverence as I often I have all ways found That Contented resignashan is ye nyest way to dilivatansbeforehad done; & I was no sooner Contented, but in three or fower weekes at most, on December ye 23e (Afore mentioned), I was taken out of this wildered place, & put into such A Calme, as is not to be Expressed :5:li:91that as, the very day & houre& meinite of my being set in the wilderness was so plainely felt, & perceived, being so different an air; ☞so the takeing out of it was as vissible. leaveing all stormes behind me, & was, as set into a Sweet still haven, & new scences given me, as one not in a body; That I felt my self quite taken out of all disturbances of outward scences & set in a new air, or another Climat, & my scences all opened to have another spirit given me, as was accompanied with new understanding, & as one which had put off an old garment, nay like one uncloathed of this mortall body, & a new body brought forth to manifestation, which Caused great joy, & Admireation, much more felt then, Can be Expressed, & in a few months after(as followeth,)there opened a view of the heavenly Caanan for which, & for the many manifestations of the Eternal love of the father, threw his son of mercyfull love & Comunicated by his hold & blessed spirit, to which I alone offer all praise, honour, Glory, power, & dominion, of things in heaven, & things in Earth, & things under ye Earth, now to whom be Eternall praise.

div1.head:
A Vision and ATransportation or ManifestasionWhether in the body, or out of the body,(as St. Paul saith) I Cannot tell, but I was often, made scencible, where my body lay, & that my eyes did Abide open, by my spirits Returne to it-
Which was Munday night March ye 17 1678/9
div1.p: Being In Contemplation of mount Zion, & earnestly longing to be in mount Zion state, and also to understand what that Extreame Agony meant which I had been in fowerteen dayes before, (as held me About hald an houre when I was In bed) it was like a dark floud Cast forth, from the dragon, which was Ready to swallow me up, but my Alone defence was prayer, Crying[sideways ladder] out^ & saying nothing Els, for the Crying [sideways ladder]^ wthout ceasinggreatness of my anguish & feare, but O Jesus, O Jesus, hide me in thy wounds, thus for the space of half an houre, till there became a most Blessed & gracious Calme:

And being very scencible, of the difficulty of overcoming, the beast, and great dragon, & to get out of the babilonish principle in our progress towards heaven, my longing grew, still stronger, to be in Mount Zion, & as I was in these desires, I thought, but what If god should Come and Appeare, to me at this Instant, upon which the flesh seemed to Retreat her earnest suit, as ^Imaginingraming to my self that the sight of god was very terrible, but faith soon Choecked these fleshly feares, by Representing that this was the place which I did groan thirst & long for & that still. I was fitted, & made meet for this Inheritance of the saints in light, I earnestly desired some Comfortable prospects and visions of that glory as other have had to encourage me dureing my wandrings in this howling wilderness, this I say I had often pressed after(till, I should Arrive at ye full fruition of the heavenly) to have some Tastes of it, to stay my holy impatience yet at the same time i was Afraid, lest the sight of such a glory: should not make it more difficult for me, to be Content to stay here, in the body & increase my thirst, even to fainting, for the liveing god: these thoughts made me power out my Request, Crying out, o stay me with flagons and Comfort me with apples; for I am sick ofwith love: and sSoon after it being then neare half an hour past Eleven at night. And as I lay looking upAB (by the spiritual eye of faith), I perfectly deiscserned a touch one the top ☜of my head, as drew my spirit out of me as yn draw a knife or sword out of a shape & it cut as it was drawn forth I felt it cut sharp as a fox eged sword And I saw paradice with the tree of life in the midst of it very pleasant, & not to be Compared to anything here below; the fruits that grew upon it were of most beautifull & pleasing Colors, the leaves were of A most fresh and lively green, the grass which grew under it was young & tender, & of a passingpleasant greene, tincture, I Could see no weeds; & all appeareinged as if it had been newly watered. yet, did not this fully satisfie me, Except I might also see ye kingdom of Christ, then was I had up higher, where I saw Jesus in ye appearance of a man, all surrounded with a most glorious light wch greatly transported me, for now, I knew I was Come to the place which I
Had so long desired to be-hold: here I stood Admireing, for some [sideways ladder] My Angell Apeared to me but I underst-nd it not.while; whilst I was here I appeared to my self,[sideways ladder] & after I appeared, as a spark of light, & according to my desire I sometimes mounted up to see Jesus, & then againe descended to paradise, all which motions were verySwift: as the light. After this I desired to see the Father, & after a little stay in the Kingdom of Christ, I was had up to god the father.

but oh! oh! oh! ye beauty! ye Glory! the splendor! the brightness! the Exceeding unexpressible glory that was there! at the sight of which I threw my self downe before it, Crying Continually for Above A Quarter of an houre; my god! my god! I am now Come to the place to which Thou hast, Called me, & which I so long desired to see o I am now Come to Enjoy thee! thee being got Above all those difficulties I had been so long wading through, viz ye Kingdom of the great dragon & Beast with this Babilonish principle I can[n]ot Express the delight I tooke to see my self Redeemed from all those Burthens, lets, & hindrances I had so long groaned under.& I saw the Dragon & the beast and Babylon lye one the Earth, the dragon was Represented of A long shape & of a Green Colour like a serpent, it had fowuer short legs the foremost appeareing the longest, it was terrible to be hold: ye very thoughts of it, since neere made me tremble it appeared like a greay Lion & seemed very eager & fierce, to finde what was become of his prey, but I feared him not, being Extreamly pleased, to see my self so safe, but soone after the beast saw me & fixed his fierce great eyes upon mee with his Jaws wide open, as on watching for the prey which was in his Sight, tho, out of his Reach. The Babylonish principle lay one ye ground, in the appearance of toys & trifles of severall sorts and aspuppets for Children, they were Represented to me as If they had been SpewedSpewed out, & therefore were not to be taken up againe, I desired also to See hell, which I saw at a distance, in the likeness of a dark % o the felt Imbrases of god the father Thee devin loveSmoaking furnace, even a thick darkness which Comprehendded not the light: Then my god told me (as I sate in a Cloud of light & in the embraces of Divine love, that I saw not Come up to Abide there, as yet, but that I was first to pass, the bryers and thorny way, Paradise being hedged about with thornes, & none Can Enter into it but by passing the same, then I looked downe to Paradise, & saw such a stony & thorny way as I had never seen before, being all stones, & no path way to be seen, nor any body walkeing in it, the stones were half as high as my self, some times it appeared all stones, some times all thornes, & those the highest appeared Impossible to pass, I Indeavored to go but Could not tell where to tread, I tooke Care that no long garment might hinder me, I thought I would Enquire of Travellers that went that way to direct me. (tho I saw none) but presently I was Checked with a stay they need a guide themselves; I ecchoed back againe, Lord send thy spirit Truth to guide me I looked very Earnestly, to see whether I Could see any, one, in the same way with me, at length I saw one, whome I knew who Came foreAB ward, tho. the way was very bad, & up hill, & I saw yt the higher she ☞Came the faster she went tho. the way seemed worse, & worse, but at
Last ye thorny way seemed to slide away & disappeare, & instead thereof appeared a pleasant river of glass which Compassed paradise, & paradise appeared; much more beautyfull & pleasant than before, then I desired to see god ye Father againe, & the Elders in heaven with there Crownes & I desired also to sit, with them, with a Crowne one my head, & I did so, & when they fell downe & praised god, I Joyned with them falling downe before ye Throne with great Joy, then I desired to behold Christ Againe, & to see his heart (as some had seen) which I Beheld flaming, with love, to the saints. then I desired to Enter into the heart of Christ, & so I did, Entering in & Comming forth againe very swiftly, for several times; after this i was desireous to Enter into the whole Christ, & presently there upon I was in ye person of Christ, where I felt & saw my self: for I saw my Eye in & threw Christs eye, & I saw my head neck & brest in Christs, as inthrew a looking glass, so I was Satisfied; yet, I desired also to see & feel whether my hand was in Christs hand, & I found it was, & I laid hold of the hand of Christ with my fingers, and it felt to the hand which touched, as if it touched anothers hand, but to ye hand which itwas touched, as if the Right hand touched tooke hold of the left ( apon wch my sperit retorned to my body & I fou[n]d my right hand hand had tuck hold of my left hand, I was much amazed for I did not think I belong to my body or shuld ever a returne to it agane, but sune was caught out of my body more swift then an Arro w:out of a Bow,) yea I saw my whole man in & through the transparent body of Christ, which sight did Cause, un-Expressable joy in me to see yt Christ was one with me, & I one in him, yt Blessed union which I had long, desired, Clearely, to understand. Then I desired to see god the father sitting on his throne of glory wth a Rainbow, ov[er] his head, this was An un Expressible great glory, & Majestie streaming forth beames like a glorious sun, tho: Infinitely transcending [reverse %] orbyt wee see here; in ourye Heavens CircumferenceOrb [reverse %] of which glory there were most beautyfull & lustrous colours, some what Resembling the Colours & Copass of a Rainbow, but far more Beautyfull; all which I beheld with great Joy & Admiration. I Desired likewiss to see Christ in his vesture dipt in blood. then was I im[m]ediatly transported caught up into his glory & I saw his Magestie Cloathed, with a loose garment ye outside of whch was the Colour of pure Blood, but ye Inside was as lined with white, which white seemed to spread it self over most of the Red; some times I was taken up with the Admireing Consideration of Christs love, whilst I saw his love, flaming heart, from which some blood streamed forth, & also severall silver Crystalline streams: after I see the son of god in this vesture of glory Apeare at the Right hand of the Father (who appeared, as before) on his throne surrounded with an un Expressible brightness & glory, & the Rainbow Encompassing all: I desired to see ye Holy spirit which I saw in the Appearance of pure Silver Crystalline streames one the left hand of the father:| then againe I saw the three, Father sonne ☜& spirit united into one great glory making one great glorious light, & I went intowith them; together with the Elders, & we were all one great light; & then Againe they Appeared three as before, & the Elders apart & I apart, & I beheld there glory, & then againe I was swallowed up like a smaller light of a greater, & Changed into the same glory severall times, but none Can Expect Expression from me, answerable to those wounders, & glory which there I Beheld they being Indeed
Beyond all Expression. Still Continuing to behold this glory I saw noe Angels, therefor desired to see them, & immediatly there were severall of them Compassing part of the throne, they were like unto transparent gold, with the faces of men, with two large golden wings comeing forth of each side of theire faces which were most glorious, after this seeing these streames come forth from the heart of Christ, as I had seen before like unto transparant silver, I asked what it was, he said it was the fire which was to purifie the saints, then I had a minde to see the wounds of Christ, & I looked one his hand, & the wound there, did Glister like the purest part of the light, which I saw in god the father, Compareing it together: thus I Aboade in this glory & would often go into the purest part of light, of god the father, & be one with the father, & then Come out againe; & Returne as often as I would, I desired to have an Antient Christian of my Acquaintance there, who I knew had for a long time desired to see this glory, yt he might Come & enter into this light, from whence god is Called ye father of lights, & a little aft[er] he Came; then I desired that one of my Children might Come up, & in some little while she Came, & then another, & so till all were Come in, & in the same order as I had desired it, first lightof all my friend entered into the pure ghlife, & then all my Childeren one after another, & as they Came up I Remembred Remembered two little Children, which died, one at 14 weekes the other at 14 dayes End, & Immediatly as soone as I began to desire it, they Came, like two bright sparks one after theanother & Entered into this great light, & be Came one with it, as a spark if swallowed up of the flame, & then Came forth againe (to wit my friend & Children which awre living, in the same order, as they went in (them furst as went in furst.) all severall yet all like one cases of bodys, seeing them altogether, & yet severall, through Each other: Then I desired to see all the saints Come up to this glory, I Contineued in the glory, beholding the Father & sonne, but had not seen the spirit for some time, haveing there for desired to see the saints. I saw them Come like a glorious white Cloud, two & two together thick & Close, a little behinde ye Right hand of Christ, & penetrated Into Christs body, & through his heart Came forth againe, & Entered into the middist of the glory of the father, as wee had before, & so [sideways ladder] them furst as went in:i: all severally yet coming all out threw each other wch was wonderfull.there passed an Innumerable Company, & they still Ascended without Ceasing, till I Ceased to be hold, & then they Came out of the father Againe, in the same order as they Entered in [sideways ladder] & all of them sate downe round the throne, which was then of a very vast largeness, ye Eld[er] & saints sitting Round it; I looked to see whether the saints had Crownes like the Elders, & I saw they had, tho I saw they had none till they were gone through Christ, into the Father, & Come forth againe; & sat downe about the throne;& their Crownes as I thought were all of a size, they sitting in great order; the bottome of the throne was like one Smooth glass, & there were many more angels then, I had seen before, all like the former, Compassing the throne one the backside(as it were)of the saints & Elders(a little above
Theire Crownes)where they might be fully seen.

Then I thought what the lamb was, which St. John speaks of in the Revelat[ions], there stood a lamb as it had been slaine, & I looked & by the midst of the throne, neare the left side, at the foot of ye father there stood as a lamb, with its Right side towards me with A bloody place in his neck, & some blood was upon the woole, as if blood had run downe from the said wound, yet it was alive, Then I desired to heare ye saints Sing, all honor, & praise, to him; that sits one ye throne, Hallelujah, but feareing, I fainted least I should not be able to beare yeso glorious a Melodie, yet hoarkned, & when I Could not heare them sing, my selfsperit sung praises, to him yt sate one the throne, but Cannot Remember it. I still beheld the glory untill it begun to descend nearer, & the nearer it Came ye less, was the light & splendor: I said, the glory is less ye nearer the earth it Comes, or is it not because my eye of faith is somewhat, dimmed; then pressed i with a streaching forewards yt faith might not faile, but that I might see ye glory, as bright as I had seen it; upon thisan, the throne disapeared & was gone & I saw the glory of thefather of lights (the glory farre Exceeding any I had seen before) like to Transparent gold, mingled with a fiery light, which shined downe to the Kingdome of the sonne; & this glorious light shined In great beauty through the Kindom of the sonne, into Paradise below it, as A Reflection of the first pure light, and it became more Beautyfull, but far then before, shedding an unExpressible beauty over all the trees & flowers which appeared all transparent.

After this, there was A sheet of light drawne before this surpassing gloruous & beautyfull light, & another little sheet seemed to descend from it like a Cloud of Light upon the thorny ground, & lay upon it & I saw it as long as I looked after it: It being now neare two in the morning when this last appeared, the whole haveing Lasted about two hours, yebut the Idea of all remained fresh with me, from first to Last.for som dayes togather After one thing was observeable yt nothing of all I desired was denied me, but ye heareing of them sing, which I desired though not without some feare, as I had done all the Rest.

There was towards the End of this vision as I came neerer the Earth A Request put up by me (finding I had nothing denied me) Lord what wilt thou doe with this nation, & straight there Appeared a hand & arme streached out toward them, with a slight moving of the hand twice, looking like the waving or putting by my Request: wth these words, Concerne not your self with that. But oh the Ravishing & unExpressible joys I felt when I sate in the delightfull Embraces of Divine love, a joy which as it Could never be apprehended by me before, so neither Can it in the least be Expressed, by me now, And how it is very observable, yt when god told me I must goe downe Againe, because I was not Come up as yet, there to abide, & I saw the beast & dragon ready to Receive me; I was not in the least displeased, neither found I any desire to the Contrary, or any feare, but found my self wrapt up in a Quiet stillness acquiescing in the will of god, with a great delight, in the present Injoym[en]t, finding my self above, the reach of evils for the present.
Severall things here are set downe, short of what they might have been Expressed, but all infinitly short of any thing that Can be any way declared.

div1.head: Wednesday Evening, June 11th 1679
div1.p: Soone after I was abed^ being perfectly Awaked, I see by thesperits eye of faith, A very pleasant still River, & Abridge went Cross it, riseing in the Middest like an arch, but narrow. I went to goe up onye stone steps as was there to goe one the bridge to A rock, I seeaw one the other side. But when I come neare A Rockto Climbe ye bridge went higher, like a Cloud or Rainbow, so that I see saw it Could not be walked one by a weighty body of flesh, but an AtheAerial body, for the bridge was A Cloud of air[e]Aire then I Contented my self to looke one the further side of the river to the Rock, & I seesaw most pleasant greens, wch grew as If they grew out of the Rock, the Rock was Exceeding high and large, It appeared more plainer to looke like a Rock, but Extream pleasant & beautifull, in great variety, & beauty but seemed like a Rock, but a Rock of wounder, the more I woundered at the Beauty, Aboundantly more Beautyfull it appeared, yet noe great light, but shaded;one the Right side of this Rock, A glorious sun Begun to Arise, but it ☞was so Exceeding Glorious, as I trembled, and Could not Behold, then it went downe, after it Arose alittle againe But I Could not bare it, so it dissapeared, though I had A desire to have borne it, & looked for it, & If I did but looke towards it it Begun to Appeare, as If it did Declare that nothing hindred its Ariseing but my weakness, as Could not bare it, & there by shews his tenderness, to Compassionate our weakness, being in bodies of thick Clay.

div1.head: Thursday June ye 12th
div1.p: Being desirous to Continew this pleasant object: & furth[er] to understand, this Rock of wounder which Idea Remained, I seesaw growing forth of this Rock, Innumerable, fruitfull trees, loaded, as it were with very large leaves, & large Pleasant fruit, like Citterons, but Red amongst it, the beauty being very plesant, & lovely, as also how it was placed by so pure still & shady River, & how carious this Rock had presented itself, the night before, still desired, to see fully, it being as it were in a shadday place, not to be perfectly perceved. After this vast high Rock had other trees, thick & Close of small leaves, & so Curious, as If it had been pure gum work, over spreading it, from the top to the Bottome, like the side of a high hill or mountain, after it appeared like pillowsers of Clouds of sea green In great heaps.

div1.head: Friday June ye 13
div1.p:
It Appeared like a sea with waves, then like a still River, 14th
ye 15th
ye 16The same Manner the next evening Being Saturday. it Appeared like a large Champian Country like A hilly Country: & Abrook Runing betweene, two hills where I seesaw the first pure River, & by this brook appeared a Rock, but not so pleasant, as that before, sometimes the Rock seemed, to be the back towards mee, & I was troubled: & it turned the pleasant side to me tewsday ye 17th it Appeared very various, like full of very small flowers some white & some Blew.

Wednesday, ye 18th. Severall flowers of green & white; & many green & white Rushes, twisted with white, as grew one the Rock, then many small flowers of white, & some of Blew, and Pleasant Coloured flowers grew up, as one looked one them, & gon Againe, And Emediatly others in there Roome, scarcely to be desernable, what flowers they were by Comeing up so Quick, & as one disapeared, others Come so Continnually full of varietie of flowers, & A swift passing a way of the hills, and heavens, but the rock stood still.

div1.head: Thursday ye 19th
div1.p: There was Athick body of Darkness, or Plate of black, as was before, A bright light, as shined under the darkness, & the sides; & lighted ye Rock, so the Rock looked transparent, with flowers of Red & white, no other Coloure, I asked why Red & white only & no other Colour Among so many flowers, it was Answered to shew the purity of the saints when washed in the blood of the lamb.

div1.head: Friday the 20th
div1.p: Still this thick body of Darkness Remained, before the light, I desired to have got Beyound the darkness but Could not.

div1.head: Saturday the 21th
div1.p:
The thick body of darkness Remained before the light, Came over me, & I was got beyound the darkness, betweene the darkness & the light, which I had much desired, & there were so pure, A skie of all Colours, as If the Rock had spred its Transparent beauty over the heavens & Earth, so that It appeared a most beautyfull landskip every where & as in A globe then Appeared the Rock, haveing full sight of it by Reason of A pure light, but yet the back seemed to me, I said why must I be, at the back of it, & not Come before to see the treasuries of Pearle; & it turned to me where there was such Treasure, of pearle, as Cannot be Expressed, over the whole side of the Rock, groeing out of it, And I seesaw my self [reverse %] goe from me, as A[reverse %] my sperit or my Angell pure body of
of oriential pearle, like all one, pure oriential pearle, it Seemed such a shining Beauty, but the back was only towards me[four dots in diamond] (the Idea of this beauty doth greatly Reioyce yt [four dots in diamond] ye back of my Angellour vile bodys shall be made like his Glorious Body.

div1.head: Sabbath Day June 22th
div1.p: I seesaw the Rock so gloriously Adorned with goodly pearles and precious stones, as it was wounderfull, to behold, so that I might glut, my sight with seeing, yett after that, Appeared something most rare for Curiosity, it was flowers of pearle, & Rich stones as grew in the shape of flowers, with the leaves, of pearle in Curious shaps.

div1.head: Munday ye 23[rd] of June.
div1.p: As I lay a wake,(for so all hath appeared) although ye Ideas Remaines in the day, aft[er] from the first to the last) this Rock still Appeareing in its full Luster, and great Riches, being loaded wth many Larger Rich Stones, & the light Appeared very spendid Afore it; in flaming streams which greatly delighted me this, Light Continued, but the Rock disappeared for sometime, & there Appeared an Alter, with Aflaming heart upon it till an Alter wth a flaming hart apon itit became a large flame, as big as the Alter, & at some distance from the Alter Appeared a most beautyfull arbour of And an Arbour of Transparont flowersall pleasant flowers, Transparent & a great length, scarce to be seen, at the farest End; the bottome, as of glass; & I looked into it, & went in, seeing threw the flowers, the light as lighted it, not as between, but as threw; variety of Coloured pure ofglass transparent flowers. I would have been made Transparent & swallowed it up in them (the beauty was so great) as I have done, some other times when greatly delighted, (as the Rock) would have been taken into it; & would sometimes goe & sett in ☞the hollow of the Rock under the shadow, to Content, me seeing I Could not be taken into it, the Alter I seesaw flame severall times, as often as I looked towards it, then I looked for the Rock & it appeared againe & the arbour Appeared various in its flowers to wt it had before, being larger & fewer greens, more whiteish with great beauty & the skies Appeared like A beauty full landskipp I was held In this about an houre at least; the first sight of the Rock was in A shady place, but it Ascended still higher & higher, as the beauty did more, fully Appeare far Above any before.

div1.head: Wednesday ye 25th of June
div1.p: Still desireing further, to behold the glorious, wounder, of the Rock, for If wee seeke, we shall finde, it appeared with greater glory: all over pearle, & a pure pleasant light, lighted it, & Came over the Rock; & tooke it into the light; so the Rock was become one with the light, then the light gave back to one side, to shew me that the rock was in the light, and the Rock appeared like, an orient ☞Pearle, & then, I understood the light, & the Rock was all on[e] glory.

Glory even, the god of glory oh great was the delight to have such a Cleare light of that Rock: which is light & love; oh the beauty of holyness I would have been taken into it: after the Rock seemed to be The Rock is became on, orientiall pearleSeverall pearls united to ye one, Rock^as all^ of one pearle, I asked how the Rock which was but one: Orientiall pearle; what shal I say of it, it is beyond Expression, no tongue Can utter it as St. Paul said, he heard things not fit to be uttered, so this glorious glory wee have not tongues fitted to Express, I am lost to goe about; to declare, or sett it forth, If you understand what glory is, then may you give A gess, to this Ravishing overpowering, splendidness, I here seaece, & Express it best, by sayingseace, nothing more but glory, glory! And be therewith silently Transported with the rayes of its beauty.

But to the Question, how this Rock of glory, being before but one pure pearle, how it appeared like many, united into one.AB It was told me, the lord was that great pearle of price, that as his pearles, were many, & yet united, into that one great pearl, It shewed, the unitie of the unitie of the saints, when they come☜ to that great Pearle of price, & were made one with him, they are made one, by being, united in the Rock, like growing out of ☞the one pearle, severally, every one, founded, & made one, wit[h] the Rock, but one severall peareles.

Then I asked why, the Rock had appeared so various, before it Came to that beauty of glory, it seeming to be as a gross thick body, at first Appearance, though beautified upon it, it was said to declare the drossiness as is in the Saints, And how thay grow into this☜ glory, by degrees, And when Come to this fullness of glory, all dross was is done Away, they were are so Clarified, that, I desired to Enter they became like Transparent with the Rock, then I desired to Enter into this glorious light, it being then like a glory of Light; but I was told this ☞light must first Enter into mee, to purifie & burne up all the dross for mee, to be purified, to Enter in to this pure light, then I desired with panting, & hungred & thirsted reaching forth,[four dots in diamond] my whole desires, & [four dots in diamond] strong desireAffections, & as I panted It came with such an over shadowing,[four dots in diamond ☞[five dots surrounding sixth dot] This was a feding on Crists flech & Drinking of his Blud.penitrating, nay[five dots surrounding sixth dot] filling; & as I Breathed forth my Earnest Suit, it still breat[h]ed in sweet fresh galls of the spirit, penitrating mee, throughout.

Then I desired the saints might felel the same, I did, & breathing out☜ desires[downward carrot] I felt, as if virtue went out to them, & I Emtied; but hasting to the fountaine, where was Enought to fill me & others, for I had only ☞what I had Receved, & wanted if breathed forth to others, but this Cane be as little Expressed, as before, I said of the Rock: but it was a sweet life, love, power, & virtue, over powering & filling mee, with Joy, delight & praise, & such an Intimate familiarity as if I might have, & doe, what I pleased, Conveverscing with god, as with ons Intimate friend, nay more as with ons Self.

div1.head: Thursday ye 26th of June
div1.p:
I seesaw like A wall, of stones of gold, in great Beauty, often Presenting its self, & haveing ye Idea of the Rock in my minde, I desired to
so understand why, A Rock had been so long Represented to me,AB And so various, the miditations were such as these.

1First why a Rock to declare it was A foundation as Cannot be shaken; 2Secondly: It being placed in a shady place, & by a River shewed, that Refreshing shelter, in the lord Jesus in the time of scorching temptation;

3Thirdly the pleasant greens, being severall, & after trees loaded with fruit, & after variety of flowers, the fullness of delight, may be Alutded to the spoues in the Canticles, I sat under, his shadow wth great delight, & his fruit was sweet to my taste.
4thFowerthly, then A Rock denotes, securitie, for sometimesthing it appeared, hollow where I did, & might sett in the hollow, and be hid, and safe, in the times of great danger.
5thFifthly then A Rock is unmoveable, so that moved not though the heavens & the Earth passed swiftly aways.

6thSixthly the Rock did usually stand with on side towards me & sometimes the back, to declare wee Cannot see but in parte, & understand but in parte, till glorified, then shall see him as hee is. 7thSeaventhly & lastly, the great treasures of pearle one the Rock to shew the Riches & treasures in god, & that he is not only so in him self, but Communicated of him self to us, was declared in my seeing my self, goe from me, as a pure body of on orientiall pearle, being made pertakers of his divine nature, as of the nature of the Rock I haveing many pearles allso growing out of this body of one Pearle; as the Rock had.

div1.head: Friday ye 27th June
div1.p: A wall of GoldThere was Continued, that wall of stones of gold, but much higher, not to be Climbed by scence, I looked upon it as the wall of the new Jerusalem, it was very glorious.

div1.head: Saturday the 28th
div1.p: This golden wall I was Raised to look over it, & seeI saw apure body of shining gold, & this did often present it self.

div1.head: Sabbath day ye 29th
div1.p: This golden wall, or wall of gold, I Could well se over it, & see the glory of that person, like bright shining gold;(& after A pleasant light very delightfull, I seesaw at our meeting, when we meet togeth[er]) after this golden wall seemed to Compass three Courts, the first was the largest, the second lesser, the third was like a Court Covered & filled with the golry of the lord, like a glorious Exceeding beauty full light.

div1.head: Munday the 30th of June
div1.p:
This Glorious light still Continued (& greatly delighted me) placed in the middist of A golden porch, being filled with the glory of ye
The lord, After appeared A most Curious Cabinet like olive woodA Cabinet Inlayed Curiously in Cutt flowers; soone after appeared A stone building of the Colour of olive wood, sut into Carved work, i was very neare itAnd a stone my eye neere touching it, to deserne it Exactly to be of stone.

div1.head: Tuesday ye First of July1679
div1.p: This building Curiously Cut, still presented, & like fower Pinacles, at Each Corner one; I said, isis this the temple of the lord, as shall be with men, & is he come to tabernacle with us, but Could not understand it, And it was descended to A large Champian, green pleasant place; (these sweet sights & visions declares, god is Coming to us, & is in spirit with us, by giveing such delights to the spirituall eye of faith, If we press after it, this Strengthned me to beg of god to give mee the Spirit of Prayer: (& as Christ when one the Earth said to the deaf & dumb bee opened:) & take my tongue & loose it, & open my blinde eyes, & there was an Imediate Answer wth A great quickning & Refreshingl & Earnest prayer with Assurance: that as he did then, let me feele his power, hee would answer mee & soone after goeing to sleep (it being after I was abed) I dreamed of much Inlargement in prayers, though some I thought Came in☜ yet I went one not the least discomposed, (I wait they time o lord being the best

div1.head: Wednesday ye 2[nd] of July
div1.p: Being very deisreous further to behold this Curious building, & it Appeared at a great distance, & not so Curiously Carved as before and went leasurely downe at one End as If it went to some part of ye globe as is against our feet, I said what is it gone to East India? I often thought one this building or temple wheter it went, desireing to understand it, but Could not (so I waited) & after there was A most a most gloryous & Butifull Lightglorious beautifull light displaying it self variously to great delight for some Considerable time together, after about a foot high, then appeared in place of there was IA high hill of fir trees all young ones About a foot Highl then appeared in place, of the fir trees, cypress trees very thick like a grove with Agoeing into it, but Could not see into it, it was so thick & shady

div1.head: Thursday ye 3[rd] of July
div1.p:
This Great Hill seemed larger, & had other trees far more beautifull then the others & over it A great light, yet it did not light the trees, though it seemed to touch them at which I woundered, but had this apprehension of it that it is was light in its Self although it lighted not them, darkness may be neare the light, yet Comprehend it not, & this light went & lay one the trees, like A sheet of light, or white Cloud, & Above this white Cloud Beyound it there was a very large Beautyfull plaine the trees beneath it Remaining, & the white Cloud, upon them, this plaine seemed
Seemed very smooth & pleasant, & at A distance a green feild with Flints, & another feild with liveing Creatures, Called Ggoats & like goats, but declared to be men, after some time this plaine was all in waveing Colours, shady greens, very pleasant, aft[er] appeared a Reddish light, that made the plaine all light of A Reddish light, & I desired to draw neare the light.. to fully see it. And as St Paul said wee shall see him, as he is, & be, like him, such a translating Sight was this, that I was taken up into it, and seesaw my self walk too & fro like, a body of light; with great satisfaction & delight; as of the same Reddish light.

A Fountainafter there was A light Coloured marble Ffountain, Curiously Cut, and Arose higher & larger to A very large fountaine, I watched very strictly, to get some of the water, but none Came forth, I looked If any small streames did appeare, for sure, I said, there is water Enough in it, & being very thirsty for some, it was said to me, the fountaine Indeed, is full, & Just Ready to run over, upon all☞ nations, this did greatly stay me, that god was very neere & Ready to Come to power out of his Spirit & to all nations, after there was like veines of a Rock Enamaled, as did winde About this fountaine, which, I tooke to be full of water, but they were Close sealed up

div1.head: Fryday ye 4th of July
div1.p: Still I thirsted for the water, out of the fountaine, that I might drink of the liveing water & be filled with the spirit, & I was had up & did drink, suping it up as Athing ready to flow over, this having been my Earnest request, pressing for it, much for A powering forth of the spirit, for the Rushing powers of the holy Ghost on us as& upon all the saints, this had been my pressing suitshoot, the day before the Appearance of this fountain being, Ready to be powered forth I tooke to be An answer to it

After to wards Evening haveing had some, prospect of a Returne of prayer Concerning some relations I resolved, in all Concerns to☞ Cast my self & mine upon the Care of god; who Can doe all things as he wills, saying let it be so, & it is so, & ever hereafter to obey those Commands (as far as the lord shall Enable mee) Casting our Care upon him, he will sustaine you, goeing to him (as Indeed he is) as to our father telling our griefs, & begging his direction, & speaking word.

div1.head: Saturday July the 5th
div1.p: Being very desireous to see theis fountain powered forth, I Considered it was told me, the fountaine was ready, I see therefore the delay is because we are not yet fit to receive, it Called me to minde thepag. 13: Ariseing of that glorious sun, at the Beginning of the Rocks appeareing which nothing hindred its a Riseing in its full strength, & luster, but my not being able to bare the Exceeding, Brightness of it being an unExpressable glory, a peircing burning fireery flame as Could not be borne.

div1.head: Sabbath day ye 6th of July.
div1.p: Still Pressing, for this fountaine to be powered forth upon all flesh, that all may behold his glory, & in particuler I might have such A measure of it, as I might declare his Immediat teaching by some Excellency in life, & soon after I seesaw this fountain so full as the water swelled up, even above the top: I Cried O break forth, for thy glory, fill our thirsty souls, why withholdest thou, seeing Enough in thy self nay as if desired to be eased, even like breasts full of milk, to be Emptied, where is the delay then☜ O lord it is in us, make us meet, fitted, vessels for this new wine of the spirit, that it may not be put into old vessels, O Lord Lord make us new throughout, O Come Lord Jesus Come Quickly fill, fill us, even so come lord Jesus, Lord are not these thy owne, Breathing in us, yea Lord I know the spirit doth groane☜ in me, with strong cries as Cannot be uttered, & there was wrought in me a firme beleife, as god would sweety breath his spirit amongst us at that time, I then being to meet, & as we were met together to seeke the lord for the more powering forth of the holy & blessed spirit of god, haveing given us the first fruits through in measure, the praise & honour be to him for any Refreshments, in this our pilgrimage.

I seesaw this fountaine appeare, beginning to run over like A precious ointment, I was greived it was so far Above our Reach, that it came not into us, it declared that anoynting oyle of the spirit, that unction from the holy one, as teacheth us all things, severall time was this fountaine thus presented which did procure great joy &, Afirme beleif that he was Comeing by the oyntment & as the spirit did thus declare in me as it was Comeing running a little over, by fitts, one the top of the fffountain, lieing like a rich oyntment, & as the spirit did thus declare in me as it was Coming, soe in our friend at ye meeting which knew nothing of that word I had, he also declared thatAnd surely ye syerif was wth us tho: we knew it not the spirit prophesied in him, he was Comeing & was sweetly Enlarged & also after in Singing of praise, with greater joyfullness then usually.

div1.head: Munday ye 7th of July
div1.p:
Haveing sweet breathing & overshadowing, from the god of all Consolation, reviveing & makeing glad the whole Inward man, I was much pressing for A Clear understanding of my work & duty, Concerning the Receiveing the Elemts of bread & wine, in a Scacramentall way, having been the day before at that ordinance, & haveing for sometime before it, begged direction, not fully understanding what neede there was of the figure, when wee had the substance, for I had fully Experienced, what it was to Eat Christs body
Body & drink his blood, & had it Revealed to me in a very high Communion, & over shadowing incomes, that this, is the Eating, Christs body & drinking his blood & Rejoyced in Spirit & said now I know what it is, this, this, is the Eating of Christs flesh this is the drinking of his blood, I feel a vitall vivefying I finde Christ is Come by his spirit, doe this Christ said till I Come.

30. Jun.It Called to minde the Cabinet I seeaw About the beginning of this month & the temple being Curiously Cut, but after not so beautyfull & ABhow it went downe & turned over to A nation against our feet, & I see a people flock to it in habit like ye Indians that there might be, an overturne of these outward formes as to us, but might be of use to Call them, as had not heard whether there was A holy ghost, but as to us, it might depart & wee shall not be left Comfortless, but he would send his spirit for in the place of it appeared the most pleasant delight full light, that words are too short to Express, & a fountaine full, &which after flowed over.

div1.head: The 8th of July
div1.p: Some Incouragements I had to hold on our way what ever wee may meet with, If we have lost house, or land for Christ, we shall by Incomes Immediatly from him, Receive In this life a[n] hundred fold; O the Refreshment in the wayes of god, the sweet delights the Ravishing Joy, in the soules Conversing with divine wisdome far Transcending all the painted pleasures, Compared with this bliss

div1.head: (Wednesday)July the 9th
div1.p: uppon serious Meditation I finde the great & last to be swallowed up of life, is the mortall scsences to be swallowed up of Immortallitie:

which wisdome doth by opening her divine treasures & Riches and beauty of holyness, to our invissible scences with various delights wch far surmounts all outward, such as eare hath not heard not eye seen, & to our feeling the overpowering, over shaddowing breathings of the spirit, & tasting of Joyes to Come, feeding one Christ.

wwe had neede keep a strickt watch against the least motion of sinfullsensitive - life, soone after these thoughts wee meet togaether, to wait one the lord, to keep that love fire warme as will put out all Earthly Affections, as ye sun puts out A fire, or darkens a Candle: I seeaw when meet to gather a pleasant green feild for sometime, but did not much observe it, of A sudden, like A sudden light for some time, where I see the most beauty full shady blew like heaps of Clouds, & white Amongst them, or A light as Reflected with such an unexpressible beauty as scensitive Colours are not to be Compared to it with A bright light by it, the Idea Remained very pleasant & About two hours after, seeing it very Cleare as at the first & the bright light by it, as a white Cloud, went leasurely over thes beautyfull pillers of blue Clouds, & from whence this light Cloud Came Arose A glorious sun as If it had, by that Ariseing dispersed ye
The white Cloud, & all become Cleare, & I see the sun as it arose till it Came to A pretty hight, ther was some little feares In me at ye first Ariseing of this sun, when this sun riseth in its strength it will make all Clouds of feareful nature to dissapeare & from our faintings will us up rear, for perfect love is without feare: The sun had a Circle round the Edges of pure streames of gold, & many people flocking to it eagerly to behold it, the ground was of gold rough like very fine gravil, the people run as if they had A desire to worship it, so hada gloryous Light ye sun compared to it was but like a small candell I, being moved thereunto, but did not, after where this gold Earth was, there Appeared such A glorious light many hundred times larger then ye sun before: And so shined that ye sun Compared to this light was but like the smalest Candle, Compared with the sun, for light or largeness, I said, what is this great light it Cannot be the Reflection of this sun asthat is newly risen, for it so far Excels it that by its Reflection & beauty darkens it, surely it Can be noe less yn ye Reflection of that glory of glories, as is Above & I see so glorious transparent light hang over it hovering in the air like a globe of light, which Reflection this great light was

div1.head: Thursday ye 10th of July
div1.p: Being in Miedditation of that sun & the beauty of it & Contemplating of the brightness of the fathers glory which was so Transparent beholding it with delight, & filled with Joy. God is all glorious, one the Right hand (look) or one ye left hand, Even not able to Containe it nor Express it, byut Causeth a holy Impatience to have mortallsye fore tast puts ye soule in a holy lounging for ye posesan Swallowed up of Immortalitie (yt I might not be thus straitned) & how am I straitned thus to be Cabined up in flesh, & not in ye Glorious libertie of the suons of god, & as Christ said, so I may truely say I have A Baptisme of the holy ghost as with fire, to be Baptized with to purge Away all dross, self, & sin, & how am I straitned till it Come O I am Even forced to say, turne Away thy Ey, for thou hast Ravished me, O when shall I be able to Containe, what thou wilt give? how long lord, holy & trewue? wee Can take in but little of glory here, we Can hold but little of this new wine by Reason of our old vessels of flesh, but yet alittle while he will Come, & we shall Enter Into glory. till then we groan within our selves, with strong Cries, for the Redemption of the body.

div1.head: Fryday ye 11th of July
div1.p:
I seesaw A pleasant walk of gravell, & trees In great Exactness, & an Ascent above it more pleasant, with severall walkes; after thereRich gates lick of ye city of Jerusalem was A rich & glorious building of aggates large & Compassed with Edges of gold as Joyned the aggates togather, it was like a^ Ggate to some great City, it being high & large, then I seeaw another gate very Rich all of moth[er] of pearle, & gold, & pillowsars of some Rich twisted Christiall, I said surely this is the gates of ye City of Jerusalem, this is like A gate-house, but If this is but like the porters lodge, what must ye palaces be? If this is but the gate to it what is the Chamber of p[re]sence
which is filled with odours of his glory? then I seesaw an open Gallery with pillers of stone or marble & speckled with gold, & one one side a wel neer-tlyreeneerful, of water, with A bucket of mother of pearl, Chained with A great Chaine to the well.

div1.head: Saturday ye 12th of July
div1.p: The Idea being very Refreshing to Admire the great Riches In god, & to Contemne allthese things besides, makeing it our business to wait on wisdomes teaching, for those beauty full discoveries bBeyond the former gatee, was another gate, like a portch with ana Rich porch arch over it, there were 6 Pillers as bare up this porch, 3 at a side & 4 outward most, of A Clear gold Colour stone, very beauty full & twisted the 2 middle most pillars of white smooth stone, like an unpollished diamond, the Cover was of divers large flat Rich stones of several Colours, & the front of the porch over it, & the sides of it were many beautifull flowers of these Rich stones, to great Admiration ye gate within, was shut, it was A dark Reddish Colour. I diligently watched to see the gate open to goe in, after some time it leaisurely opened & at the farthest side of the porch, there was shSuch another gate shut, I finding the first opened. not till some Considerable time & at first alittle, so by degrees, made me think I should not see this opened, & then Considered that I desired to have it open, to goe in but alas, I must not stay there, O lord to goe in & there Abide, Lord when shall it once be? when Come to A state of fixation & no more goe back againe, to the Ruins, ruinous places of this world, & finding my self greatly burthened, at this state of absence, yea a holy Impatience, but towards night the next day I became as one still, & said, I bless thee yt thou dost declare, thy beauty, & Excellencie as Refreshing Cordials in this wilderness Even wine of Consolation, but O when to the state of posession of father sonne & spirit.

div1.head: Sabbath day ye 13th of July
div1.p:
At night after I was abed,( as for the most part then is theThe soule is comforted in its prez present fore tacst & vew of its inheritans. sweetest Incomes,) I praid & obtained a sweet Aquissence in god I Considered the great mercie, I Enjoyed by this opening & visions of glory & therefore ought to bless god, O that here by we may be In heavenly Enjoyments before our time, I meane by vewing o[ur] Inheritance before our posession, seeing our heir ship, that althought we have not yet ye purchased, possession yet may greatly Rejoyce to see what wee are Redeemed to, surely Joy & sorrow is very Consistaent with our present state, to Rejoyce in hope by O our groanings may well be borne with, & doubtless are pleasing to the☞ father of all Consolation, & he yt heares our groans will Come to help, & stay our longings, yea even faintings under our burdens of flesh. O wee know not how any longer to debase our selves, help us to that birth of power under our strong Cries, for deliverance that thy Kingdome, may Come, thy will may be done in us as it is in heaven.aft[er]
After this I found A sweet stil quietness to Rejoyce in the presaent visions & declarations of Glory, his will being our great Glory, for then wee are glorified, when wee Can stand still in his will.☜ Then I seesaw ye Inward gate; asthat was shut, opened wide, & it was filled with A white Cloud of smoak, as with the glory of god soone after this Cloud was Cleared Away & like A long Entrance there went from this Rich gate, in shape like an aArbour, soAn Arbour of rich stons in variaty of colered flowers Rich with all varietie of Coloured Rich stones, In flowers all Transparent, And so long as I Could not see to the End, though I went into it; it appeared after various with great treasure and beauty, like Indeed, as a passage belonging to such Rich gates, & porch as was before.

div1.head: Munday July ye 14th
div1.p: I seesaw this porch with the Entrance to it, like an Arbour very long, & at the farthest end, there powered downe great heaps, of gold pebbels, & being very Exact to see what wasgold pebbels for ye pavemet done with them, they were all laid as the pavement of this beauty full arbour far surmounting all the Riches of this world.

div1.head: Tuesday, July ye 15th
div1.p: It was much upon my minde a well as I had seen, at the firsta well of water & a bucket of mother of pearl chained to it seeing of these gates, being full of water, & a bucket of mother of pearle Chained to the well, this Rich bBucket sure is fFaith, Chained by lLove, to the well, as we may goe & draw water, of life & strength virtue, power, out of the well of salvation, O strong bands of love as holds us, I mean gods love, who loved us, first, Causeth us to love him, After this I seesaw Rich beautyfull stones, like a wall beginning to appeare after like A stone, Cut like a Coate of maile, it was not to be peirced between, but all one stone, & beyond it like a beautyfulla stone Cut like a Coat of Maile wch arose to the hith of a mountaine shewing the securitie and safety in god arbour & this stone Arose to an Exceeding height to ye hitht of a mountaine, as did greatly Rejoyce, & strengthened me the securitie & safety as was in god, he is a strong hold, a sure Refuge from Stormes & theywee still finde it, who put theire trust whole strength & trust, under ye shadow of his wings of power.

div1.head: Wednesday July ye 16th
div1.p:
Considering of this wall & of this well, O the strong Chaine of gods love as holds the bucket of faith to the well, gods love & ours is so linked togather gods love is the Chaine of the strong power of god to enable us by faith, to fetch strength life & power out of the wel of all Comforts, O yt love of god, wee are kept by the mighty power the Chaine of love power, through faith, to salvation, the love of Christ Constrains to obedience, to doe his will that we may have the purchace & posession, which posession is no less then him self, glorified with the father, he in the father, & wee in him O that blessed union the Earnest & fervent love we have for this union, Causeth these groanings yea Even faintings for god,
for the living god, O when shall wee Come & appeare before him to see him as he is, eye to eye, our vaile of flesh Changed, & be made like his glorious body, yt ye love where with god hath loved Christ may be in us, & he in us, now Christ in us is the hope of glory, but then we shall be in Christ in the possession; O never, never to Returne to feed on visions, but come to fruition; At night I seesaw yt mighty Stone wall all as of one stone, like A mountaine it declared to me god was A strong Refuge, whoat Could peirce this wall, what Cannon Could Enter Into it, or Above it it greatly delighted the safety in this bulwark, i, asked who were there, sure thy must be Eminent Saints, such as Abraham & the Prophits, asthat were so secured, it was said to me it is my hiding place for the saints; surely Abraham is there, IAB thought, & as Abraham offered up his only sone, ye son of theto offer up our Isaac ye complet ment of our worck in this Body: blessing, O lord I offer my self to thee, my Isaac the blessing aswch I desire to Receve,(which is A body here to gloryfy thee in; an Evangelical body, but thy will be done it is the blessing, ye Compleating the worke of Redemption here, yet I will offer this desired blessing on the Alter of thy will, & am willing to live or dye a dulledgedeludge of destruction being Ready as wee think to over take us, & I, ytthought I offered my blessing Isaac, laying it one an alter to dye; to goe to this glory, being Just by it; and the great wall gave back, & I seesaw many people in it, such as wee are In bodys of flesh, & I was taken in, there indeed was A hiding place till the storme was past.

A place of securitie, & it Compassed them round & over them asyt they Could not be seen, & after a little while it opened againe & ye people went out, some to ye Right hand, & some to the left, a very great Company, & the great wall did goe Away by degrees, with them, diffusing itself in a thin CLoud of air, not much to be deiscerned, but went by degrees, as they went, to declare gods Special presence ytas followed them, that where they were he was, & they went not out till his presence went with them, the presence of god, over shadowing ytus (though invisibile as to man) is such a defence as that bulwark seemed when it was at that great strength, & after they were gone there was A feild like A Gardners ground newly planted with herbs, & little bushes like gooseberry trees, with their young leaves as in the spring, and A place ploughed up in the middest of the feild.

div1.head: Fryday July ye 18th
div1.p: The over shadowing of the almighty power of god is our defence though an host should Compass us about, In him is our securitie who is A wounder working god.

At night after I was Abed, I seesaw pleasant gravel walks & grass betweene with great Exactness,& pleasantness then some trees and beyound it many trees like a woode, after feilds & a swift passing of the heavens & Earth away for some time, & then A pleasant stillness all looking very delightfull, like a pleasant skie reflecting the same one the Earth, & large branches of flaggs growing red & white, & many saints, like departed saints in white, And at ye side A glimmering white light as I was Refressed at.

div1.head: Sabbath day ye 20th of July
div1.p: When wee were meett together(as usually our Costume is)when one was singing a himn of praise,)& I seesaw a small dore open, & A plesant Ascent of hills like as they were of mettals of various Coloure as of gold, others of them as of all silver, some like mixed, & above it brake forth A pleasant light, by degrees, that it might be, the better borne; After At night there was A very pleasant place much like the other, but more larger, & a beauty full landskip & a greater glorie of light, but there was A thick dark body Like a plate of darkness wch shadowed the light from me, & being very desirous to get near the light, I pressed to get beyound the dark, & I got beyound it, & the dark plate seemed to rub Against☜ of the plate of darkness as rub against my head my head as one going under A low dore, & then A Cleare light noe shadow, betweene, which greatly Rejoyced me.

div1.head: Monday ye 21th of July
div1.p: Seeing A beauty fill Landskip of feilds but when neare them they were all of pure gold & Rough Cast, & there shined such a pure Cleare strong light on this gold that the very Reflection, as lay onec the grounds, looked like A glorious Soun, in its full strength, this light asthat shined so bright Came from an opening in the Clouds like A dore or window, which place within was all day light like all☜ a dore openedin thot plase wos all day, I say Lick all sunn a globe of all Bright glory one Sun, A globe of all Light; A globe of all bright glory, the globe of the Earth like nothing to it, for greatness, The sun wch lighteth our heavens here: lookes like A bright spot to light, the heavens being many times larger.

☞But there the heavens was all soun, which glory Could not be beheld but that it opened but a little, O what glorified persons shall wee then be, when made able to behold pure deity, O this is the Eternity of glory, no Comprehending the vastness, this was pure deity, which wee are sparks of, here ye trinity is in unity, & unity in trinity, her is in this light, heat, virtue, & power, light, in god the father, who is the father of light, virtue in his sonne, & power in his spirit, by which we Receive vivefying life, virtue & power, to subdue, all our wills, to himself.

div1.head: Tuesday ye 22 of July
div1.p:
Being much In Contemplation of gods power who is able to p[er]fect what he hath begun, & will to ye day of Redempton, with miditation & Consideration how god worked at first on me before I was Eighteene yeares of age & the doubts I lay under for 6.months & thenpg ye 3d after how I fell sick; & seesaw all my sins as one act write before me & hell opened, to Receive me which I looked upon as most due, but after, how god Came in with free grace & mercy, with the witness of his Spirit applying several places of Scripture, no longer to be disputed Against, Comeing with such A Comfortable-ing power, & how ye heaven was
pag: 4:opened & an Angell Ready to Receive me (which is mentioned more at large in the beginning of ye book

I was also Considering what figure I seesaw then, & Immediately I seesaw the skie open, & a most pleasant beautyfull angel as if Cloathed with flesh, which I Remembred I had then seen yt stood Ready to Receive me, this I looked, one as only A vew of what I had seen, heretofore Abouet 20 yeares past.
Hereuppon I wase Requesting holyness throughout being the fine linnen of the saints

And had some feares, least this state I was in might not Continew; therefore desired to be with god, to behold all his wounders & glory, & I seesaw A pleasant Ascent very upright like A skie, where parte of it was like ye Colours of a Rainebows, and Alight, & by it I seesaw an opening in the heavens, where was one In figure like A man Child, as I did Judge; it was most beautyfull, a little like the former as is mentioned, but Larger, Round his head was like a sun, streaming out, he was Compassed as in an Oval much of the Colour of A Rainbow, I was told that☞ was me, I was Come up; & I might be sure I was there, because I Could see my self there, & that this was to declare, & that this was to declare to me, to Assure me yt as sure as I seesaw that there, so sure I was there; & that you are Circled in a Circle of security free from danger, I thought yt was not me for I was am In my body, iIt was said, your body, you know is not the man, thats but the shell (& I thought I seesaw my self Like A shell,) but the man is the desire, will, & Affections, thats the whole of man, & that☞ yow see here, therefor you are here, & so Circled with desire divine power: to keep the whole man up, with the lord, this did greatly stay, the Circle was thick, though of the Colour of a Rainbow, the Circle of securitie, is my great support, & It Called me to mind, that I had no such Cause to feare the loss of these Injoyments;
